questions.q: What is the primary purpose of backpropagation?
questions.why: Backpropagation computes how much each weight contributed to the error, so the network knows which direction to adjust each weight.

questions.q: Which function is commonly used to introduce non-linearity in a neural network?
questions.why: Activation functions (like ReLU or sigmoid) let the network model non-linear relationships.

questions.q: What does a single neuron compute before applying its activation function?
options: A weighted sum of its inputs plus a bias
The loss of the entire network
questions.why: Each neuron computes a weighted sum of inputs plus a bias term, then passes that through an activation function.

questions.q: What is a Convolutional Neural Network primarily used for?
questions.why: CNNs use convolutional filters that are especially effective on grid-structured data like images.

questions.q: What problem does gradient descent solve?
options: Finding weights that minimize the loss function
questions.why: Gradient descent iteratively updates weights in the direction that reduces the loss.

When a model has too few parameters
questions.why: Overfitting happens when a model memorizes training data patterns that don't generalize to unseen data.

questions.q: What is the order of the equation dy/dx + y = x?
questions.why: The order of a differential equation is the highest derivative present — here it's the first derivative.

questions.q: Which method is commonly used to solve first-order linear ODEs?
questions.why: The integrating factor method is the standard technique for solving first-order linear differential equations.

questions.q: A separable differential equation can be written as:
questions.why: Separable equations can be rearranged so each variable and its differential are on opposite sides.

questions.q: What is the general solution form of a homogeneous linear ODE with constant coefficients?
options: A combination of exponential terms based on the roots
questions.why: The solution is built from exponential terms e^(rt), where r are roots of the characteristic equation.

questions.q: What quantity describes the rate of change of velocity?
questions.why: Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity with respect to time.
Newton's First Law is the law of inertia — an object stays at rest or in uniform motion unless acted on by a force.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.why: Force is measured in Newtons (N), defined as kg·m/s².

questions.q: What does breadth-first search explore first?
options: All nodes at the current depth
questions.why: Breadth-first search expands all nodes at the current depth level before moving deeper.

questions.q: What guides a heuristic search algorithm?
options: An estimate of cost to reach the goal
questions.why: Heuristic search uses an estimate (heuristic function) of how close a node is to the goal to guide exploration.
